body:
Can you try adding `--disable ListR` to your `rclone size` command and see if you get the same answer?

Is this a shared drive?

Might it have duplicates? Can you check with `rclone dedupe`?

Can you do

```
rclone-v1.50 lsf -R drive: | sort > old
rclone-v1.51 lsf -R drive: | sort > new
comm -13 old new > extra
```

and examine the extra file to see what the extra files are

> I've lost some of the files after doing `rclone dedupe` (because they were in "My Computer" zone added to "My Drive", so files deleted in one place are also deleted in the other).

I'm sorry to hear that.

Are these files effectively hard links then? In the same directory? How did that happen?

Maybe I should test if the files have the same ID before and don't delete them if they do.

Or alternatively I should be unlinking them from the directory instead: See #3998 for similar issue.

> but it would be great if, by default, you make dedupe not delete duplicates, just list them and ask for confirmation.

At the moment it prompts for most things but it doesn't prompt for identical files (with the same checksum) in the same directory :-(

@ncw The files I lost were all added to "My Drive" from "My Computers", with "My Computer" holding the files backed up by Backup & Sync.

Probably the ID thing should solve this. Cool to see then that this might have a positive effect in rclone and it won't be for nothing :)

EDIT: Hmm, just wondering I might be wrong... Everytime I added a folder from "My Computer" to "My Drive", whenever a new file was added to the "My Computer" folder, the linked folder in "My Drive" would mirror it and appear there as well. In "My Drive" I kept a really similar structure of "My Computers" structure. However, many times I linked the file I just added to My Drive before checking if it was already mirrored. This made me ending up having two exact copies in "My Drive". In order to fix that, I simply drag and dropped the file to the linked folder (which already contained a link to the file as I said before) and it was fixed that way, only appearing once in the folder (and not twice) as basically the link and the file was only one.

Can you test both possibilities in your end in order to see if you can reproduce? I hope you understood what I mean, the setup is somewhat complex to figure out. What a mess Google did with the "Computers" tab.
